description.narrative: Centres d'études, Economiques et Sociale de l'Afrique de l'Ouest-Pôle Régional Niger Niger, a landlocked Sahelian country in West Africa, has a population of around 26,312,034 (source, INS projection, July 2024), over 81% of which is agricultural and rural. Niger faces recurrent security crises, characterized by the presence of violent terrorist and extremist groups, including self-defense groups in northern Tillabéry (on the Mali border), as well as numerous structural challenges and the devastating impacts of climate change. These changes are reflected in a weakening of governance and a reduction in arable land and pastoral areas, exacerbating pressure and competition for natural resources. On the national political front, the country was strongly affected by the coup d'état ofJuly 26, 2023 and the seizure of power by the military, causing a breakdown in the constitutional order. Economic and financial sanctions imposed by regional institutions (ECOWAS and UEMOA), superimposed on the suspension or restriction by many international partners of their cooperation and public development aid, have created a major shortfall in the government's ability to implement publicdevelopment policies for the benefit of the population. The Dosso region targeted bythe project has a population of 3,172,614, including 1,565,746 men and 1,606,898 women (source INS projection July 2024), the majority of whom are young. The population is made upof Zarma, Haoussa, Peulh and Touareg. The main economic activities are agriculture, livestock breeding and trade. The main sectors of activity identified in the Dogondoutchi, Dosso and Tibiri departments are agriculture and livestock breeding, and to a lesser extent fishing, gathering and trade (processing of agricultural products). Population movements and the high rate of demographic growthare having a double impact on agropastoral systems, leading to competition for access to and use of natural resources. The impact of climate change is another aggravating factor (uneven spatio-temporal distribution of rainfall, flooding, prolonged drought, lack of water points, etc.). This fragile context particularly affects young people, as well as the more vulnerable women in Niger society: limited access to land ownership, credit and agricultural inputs, low representation in decision-making structures, limited accessto training opportunities and technology, etc.In this delicate context of political crisis, insecurity and climate change, it is necessary to support several initiatives, in a coherent, integrated and rapid manner, aimed at strengthening governance to guarantee the delivery of administrative and social services to the population, offering economic opportunities to women and young people, and working to consolidate peace and strengthen community cohesion to preserve social and cultural norms. Problem definition:The combination of a security crisis, climate change and poor access to basic services frequently leads to the outbreak of inter/intra-community conflicts, which take various forms: suspicion and stigmatization based on the ethnic variable, increasingly marked religious and cultural identities, questioning the legitimacy of the authority of traditional chiefs in conflict management. Young women and men under the age of 30, who account for 74.82% of the Nigerien population (PDR 2016-2020), are more vulnerable and affected by these tensions, which translate into acts of incivism or exploitation towards them. The development of the modern private sector, capable of accompanying the diversification of the Niger economy and necessary for inclusive growth, thus remains a major challenge. The overall unemployment rate is rising, from 13% in 2011 to 17% in 2014. The incidence of unemployment is higher among women than men, with respective levels of 28.9% and 4.4% in 2014. It is also more marked among young people, with an unemployment rate of 23.7% for the 15-29 age bracket. Underemployment affects 68.4% of the working population. It is most prevalent in rural areas, affecting 70.4% of the working population (PDES, 2017-2021). The displacement of populations also accentuates youth unemployment due to the abandonment of economic activities in the localities of origin and the reduction in trade opportunities. Difficulties in accessing finance for young people with projects are a major constraint on the development of sustainable economic activities. Access to credit is subject to rigid conditions, excluding many young people and women from the banking circuit. In addition, the lack of quality technical and vocational training and its inadequacy in relation to market needs, as well as the strong gender inequality in access to training, reduce the economic prospects of young people, especially girls. Moreover, the current context also points to a low level of involvement of young women and men in formal and informal decision-making and governance bodies. Taking socio-cultural factors into account, it has been observed that even if young people are present in decision-making bodies, they occupy few or no strategic positions, andhave little decision-making power and influence. This inequality is all the more perceptible among young women, whose exclusion canbe exacerbated by situations of vulnerability (disability, displaced status, etc.). Yet access to decision-making positions is likely to (1) ensure that the needs of the social group are taken into account in public policies, and (2) encourage the creation of youth-led initiatives. This low level of participation helps to crystallize the gap between those with political power and young people, which can lead to frustrations that undermine social cohesion, as well as increasing their vulnerability and risk of abuse and recruitment into criminal networks and violent extremist groups. Empowering young women and men and making them responsible for conflict prevention and management are two key factors in strengthening social cohesion now and in the future. Building the technical and managerial capacities of young women and menis a priority in this respect, with a view to increasing opportunities for the development of income-generating activities (IGAs).To meet these challenges and make young people a real spearhead of the Niger economy, several strategies have been put in place by the State and its development partners in favor of young people.These include the National Youth Policy and the National Strategic Framework for the Promotion of Youth Entrepreneurship.The proposed project will contribute tothe following Sustainable Development Goals:SDG1: eradicate poverty in all its forms, everywhere in the world. In particular: ODD1.1 (relating to extreme poverty) and ODD1.5 (relating to vulnerability); ODD5: achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls; ODD8: promote sustained, shared and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all.In particular: ODD8.3 (on the development of VSEs and SMEs) and ODD8.4 (on the efficient use of resources); ODD16: promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, ensure access to justice for all, and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels. In particular: ODD16.1 (on reducing violence) and 16.7 (on inclusive decision-making). Planned activities take gender inequalities into account, particularly in terms of vulnerability and access to training.

participating-org.narrative: The Centers of Economic and Social studies of West Africa-Regional Pole Niger (CESAO In French)was installed in 2004 and regularly registered under number 034 / MISPD / ACR / DGAPJDLP of 17 January 2018, and covers from a statutory point of view four (4)countriesthat are: Niger, Benin, Chad and Nigeria. Nevertheless, at this date all interventions are concentrated in Niger where the CESAO-Niger Regional Pole enjoys official recognition. The CESAO-PRN is from the associative point of view headed by a Council of Orientation and Management (COG) which is the decision-making and orientation body. It now has solid experience in the development of agro-silvo-pastoral sectors, good governance and management of natural resources, peaceful resolution of conflicts and rural entrepreneurship and organizational support for rural producers, through the implementation of implementation of several projects and the delivery of services. Its mission is "to work for economic and social development of the rural and peri-urban environment by strengthening the capacities of local actors to promote themselves and to build an environment of peace, justice, tolerance and solidarity". The aimis to promote an equitable, organized society capable of leading its own viable economic activities and defending its interests. CESAO invests in the self-promotion of individuals and groups, especially in rural and peri-urban areas. In addition, from its headquarters based in Niamey, the CESAO-Niger Regional Pole has three (3) operational antennas throughout the territory namely: the Tillabéri antenna located in Tera, the Dosso antenna and finally that from Maradi.
